title: Hornet's last fight
photoNote: A Japanese dive bomber trails smoke as it dives on USS Hornet, morning of 26 October 1942. U.S. Navy, NARA 80-G-33947, public domain.
body:
Six months after she carried the Doolittle Raiders to bomb Tokyo, USS Hornet was fighting for her life.

26 October 1942. Near the Santa Cruz Islands, American and Japanese carriers traded air strikes in the long fight for Guadalcanal. In the morning attack, a Japanese dive bomber trailing smoke struck Hornet's stack. Bombs and torpedoes hit her too, and soon the carrier was dead in the water.

This photo catches that dive, a single plane coming down through a sky full of bursting flak.

American destroyers tried to sink the wrecked carrier with torpedoes and gunfire. She would not go down. That night Japanese destroyers arrived and finished her.

On paper Japan won the day. It sank a carrier and damaged Enterprise. But it lost about 100 aircraft and many of its most experienced crews, and its carriers were out of action when the decisive naval battle at Guadalcanal came less than three weeks later.

#OnThisDay #WW2
